sarah.k: Heads-up — while triaging a customer report I noticed missing audit events for a scope change right after a KMS rekey yesterday. The KMS rotation finished at 2026-03-18 03:12:00 UTC. The customer’s API key briefly allowed embeddings->chat calls for ~20m but there are NO 'scope_change' audit events in the audit index for that key. Filing here before I dig deeper.

raj: Can you paste the timeline and the key id? Also any request IDs you have from the window?

sarah.k: Key id: key_7f2b. Timeline: rotation complete 03:12, first anomalous request seen 03:17 (request_id 4c3a9f), last seen 03:37. I pulled the raw request log for 4c3a9f and the auth path shows scope_check: PASS but the audit pipeline shows nothing.

natalie: I looked at the audit-bot alerts; it triggered a generic 'rotate-complete' notif but the audit ingestion shows an empty batch for that key id. Here's the snippet I grabbed from the request log: 

```
[2026-03-18T03:17:12Z] request_id=4c3a9f path=/v1/embeddings model=text-embed-002 api_key=key_7f2b auth.scope_check=PASS route=embeddings -> routed_to_chat=false
```

alex: Hmm. Our scope-eval flow relies on cached KMS metadata tags (key->allowed_routes) to avoid a roundtrip on every auth. If the cache invalidation and the KMS rekey event were out-of-order, the auth path might have read stale "allowlist empty" or an interim state. That could cause permissive behavior until a subsequent refresh.

audit-bot: [automated] rotation-complete: key_7f2b rekeyed by devops at 2026-03-18T03:12:00Z. Audit ingestion count for key_7f2b in window 03:12-03:40: 0 events.

devops-bot: [automated] kms-rotate: key_7f2b rotation job finished (job_id=kms-rot-998). No errors reported by the KMS agent.

raj: Two immediate asks: (1) minimal repro steps so infra can replicate in staging, (2) short mitigation to prevent further scope leakage.

sarah.k: Mitigation proposal: temporarily mark key_7f2b as disabled in auth DB (quick), and push an emergency policy that treats any request that occurs within 5m of a KMS rekey as "re-evaluate offline" — basically deny until explicit re-eval. Not ideal but buys time.

alex: For a proper fix we should: 1) ensure rotation events invalidate the auth metadata cache before rotation job reports completion; 2) add a strong assertion in the auth path that any rekey timestamp > cache.refresh_ts triggers a synchronous KMS fetch (no stale pass). I'll open a PR for the assertion.

natalie: I can take the hotfix to flip the re-eval toggle in runtime config and run a backfill to synthesize audit events from request logs for the missing window. Backfill command I'll run: 

```bash
python infra/tools/audit_backfill.py --key key_7f2b --start "2026-03-18T03:12:00Z" --end "2026-03-18T03:40:00Z" --source request-logs --dry-run
```

raj: Assign hotfix and backfill to natalie. Add incident if we can't confirm backfill + hotfix within 1 hour. Also tag legal/compliance for potential customer impact.

sarah.k: I'll notify the customer and open an incident ticket: INC-2026-0318-authz-auditgap. We should also stash the raw request_ids so compliance can verify.

alex: Quick note — check the KMS agent's node-level clock skew logs. We had one node with 35s drift last month that caused ordering issues for event consumption. If the rotate event was acknowledged out-of-order, that would explain missing invalidation.

audit-bot: [automated] incident created INC-2026-0318-authz-auditgap by sarah.k

natalie: Starting the dry-run backfill now. If dry-run looks good I'll run the real backfill and then post results.

raj: Thanks. Keep updates here. If anyone finds a clear repro please include exact server ids and the agent logs (kms-agent, auth-cache).

sarah.k: ack :thumbsup:

alex: I'll draft the PR for the cache invalidation assertion and tag @natalie for review.

natalie: FYI dry-run found 6 requests in the window that lacked audit events. Will proceed with real run in 10m.

sarah.k: Great — after backfill + hotfix we'll do a quick postmortem and add a regression test in our infra-e2e for rekey->auth ordering.

raj: Agreed. Thanks team. :pray:
